title: Textile Industry
description: Ozonation in textiles helps lower water and chemical use in fabric finishing and supports treatment of complex dyed wastewater.

textile-processing.title: Ozone in textile processing: countries, companies, and verified results
textile-processing.shortDesc: How ozone is used in jeans fabric finishing, which countries and companies already deploy it, and what studies show
textile-processing.heroText: In textiles, ozone is mainly used in two areas: fabric finishing (especially jeans fabric) and polishing treatment of colored wastewater. Below are practical cases and studies with verifiable sources.

textile-processing.content:
Ozone in textiles is not a single operation but a set of engineering solutions: ozone cabinets and drums for finishing, plus ozone loops in wastewater treatment. Factories usually introduce it where they need lower water and chemistry use and more stable lot-to-lot quality.

The practical effect depends on the exact line, recipe, fabric, and automation level. The right approach is pilot first, KPI measurement second, and only then full-scale rollout.
benefits: Lower water use in jeans fabric and dyed fabric finishing
Reduced dependence on aggressive chemicals in part of operations
Lower color and toxicity load in difficult wastewater streams under correct process design
Easier alignment with brand sustainability requirements
Step-by-step deployment without stopping the whole factory

intro.paragraph1: Textile manufacturing is highly resource-intensive, especially in wet processing and finishing. That is why ozone technologies are growing as an alternative to part of conventional chlorine-based and other oxidative treatments.
intro.paragraph2: In practice, ozone is used for finishing (jeans fabric, vintage effects, shade correction) and for wastewater treatment (decolorization, oxidation of persistent organics, and toxicity reduction before biological stages).

protocol.title: Technology framework:
protocol.text: Ozone is delivered into a sealed system with control of concentration, exposure time, humidity, and temperature. After treatment, residual ozone is destructed and safe ventilation is ensured. For wastewater, ozonation is usually integrated into a combined scheme (biology + AOP).

note.title: Important:
note.text: Some indicators (for example, “up to 95% water savings”) refer to specific processes and machine configurations. Validate all parameters on your own pilot line before full investment.

scheme.title: Recommended implementation sequence at a factory

steps.title: Audit the current line
steps.description: Measure baseline water, energy, chemicals, rejects, and wastewater treatment KPIs.

steps.title: Run a pilot on one process
steps.description: Launch ozone on one operation (for example, jeans fabric finishing) and compare quality to the baseline.

steps.title: Parallel quality control
steps.description: Track shade, strength, lot repeatability, and cycle time under real production conditions.

steps.title: Integrate safety
steps.description: Deploy leak sensors, ozone destruct unit, ventilation, and access interlocks.

steps.title: Extend to ETP if needed
steps.description: Add ozonation into wastewater treatment as a dedicated process block when required.

steps.title: Scale up
steps.description: After KPI confirmation, expand to more processes and lock settings in SOPs.
